title: Rav Manyumi bar Chilkiah
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: We find in Menachot 32b: Rav Manyumi bar Chilkiah said that Rav Chama bar Gurya said in the name of Rav — and Rav Manyumi bar Chilkiah himself said, etc. And in Yoma 2a: Rav Manyumi bar Chilkiah said that Rabbi Machasya bar Idi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.

Hyman states that in the time of Rabbah and Rav Nachman he was already a leading figure of the generation and was considered a colleague of theirs, as in Gittin 57a: Rav Manyumi bar Chilkiah, Rav Chilkiah bar Tuvia, and Rav Huna bar Chiya were sitting together; they said, if anyone has heard an account concerning Kfar Sechania of Egypt, let him say it. And it is known that Rav Huna bar Chiya was the leading figure of the generation in Pumbedita in the time of Rabbah, as explained in his entry.

And we find in Bava Metzia 66a that Rav Nachman said to Rava: I say that a conditional undertaking (asmachta) is binding, but Manyumi says that an asmachta is not binding. Hyman maintains that without doubt this is Manyumi bar Chilkiah.
As for what the Yuchasin writes, that he lived in the time of Rav, Hyman explains that he means his father Chilkiah, as is known to be the manner of the Yuchasin.

notes.text: The named vocalized Davidson text at Yoma2a explicitly names Rabbi Yochanan in the final transmission link. Hyman’s identification of the Manyumi in Bava Metzia and his explanation of Yuchasin remain his conclusions.

The inspected Yoma 2a chain explicitly reads Rabbi Machasya bar Idi reporting Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman’s leading-generation chronology, undoubtedly identification of the Manyumi in Bava Metzia, and explanation that Yuchasin refers to his father remain his arguments; the exact Yuchasin edition was not inspected.
